app.title: Rare IEM Screening AI: two-tier screening of mass-spec feature tables with a specialist review queue
app.summary: The person uploads a mass-spec feature table (one row per sample), or uses the bundled example. Each sample is scored automatically: a classic cut-off flags it first, then a trained model re-ranks those flags. Counts of screened, high-risk and low-risk samples appear above a results table where high-risk rows are highlighted. Each high-risk sample then goes into a review queue that shows its risk score, the disorder suspected and its key abnormal analytes. The reviewer confirms and refers the sample, rejects it as an analytical artefact, or asks for a repeat sample, and every decision is added to a timestamped audit trail that can be exported as CSV.

task.text: Screen a batch of samples for high risk of a rare disease and have a specialist confirm, reject or re-sample each flagged one, with an exportable audit log of the decisions.

data.text: A table of LC-HR-MS feature intensities: each row is a sample in a batch, each column is an anonymous feature. A separate feature metadata file gives each feature's m/z and retention time. The model turns this into a risk score, a call, a suspected disorder and abnormal analytes for each sample, and the reviewer adds decisions.
data.item: one sample's row of metabolite feature intensities, with its computed risk call

stage.text: reviewing flagged screening samples after mass-spec processing, before referral for diagnostic testing

mechanism.text: A sidebar describes the two-tier model and takes the uploaded table. The main page then shows summary counts and a results table with high-risk rows highlighted. Below it, each high-risk sample opens in an expandable card with three decision buttons, and each click is added to an audit-trail table that can be exported.

field.text: two-tier newborn screening of LC-HR-MS metabolite profiles in clinical biochemistry

workflow.name: flag items with a model and have a person decide on each flag, with an audit log

steps.here: Upload a CSV feature table in the sidebar, or use the bundled example table, which can also be downloaded as a template

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Each sample is annotated, normalised and turned into z-scores, ratios and pathway features. A cut-off sets the tier-1 flag, a model re-ranks the flags into a high- or low-risk call, and the sample gets a suspected disorder

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: Counts of samples screened, high risk and low risk appear above a full results table with high-risk rows tinted

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: Each high-risk sample appears as an expandable card showing its ID, risk score, suspected disorder and key abnormal analytes (|z|>=3), with a checklist of what to check in the raw spectra

steps.step: decide keep or drop for each item, with a reason
steps.here: Three buttons: confirm and refer for a diagnostic test, reject as an analytical artefact, or request a repeat sample
Every decision is appended with sample ID and timestamp to an audit-trail table
Export audit log downloads the decisions as review_audit_log.csv

distinctive: Screening runs in two tiers: a classic cut-off on primary markers (above the 99.5th centile of healthy controls) flags samples, and a model re-ranks only those flags to cut false positives
Only the model's high-risk calls go to the human queue; every one must be checked on the raw spectra before any action
Each flag is explained by the analytes whose robust z-scores against a healthy reference population are abnormal, plus the most likely disorder
One of the three decisions is to reject the flag as an analytical artefact rather than a true result, and another is to ask for a repeat sample
Decisions are kept as a timestamped audit trail, not as labels on the samples
